items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: So I stayed right there with Papa Celestine. He had Ernest Kelly playing trauma with him. And Papa was improving himself then. The guy, Kelly, and myself, and him, made good. So I stayed right there with Papa until things got good and bad, good and bad.

ctx.x: Yeah, I knew him in New York too. Nice guy.

And we stuck around there, old Frankie Dooson. Stayed there a little while. So here comes Walter Deku. Next block from the woman to play at the bungalow. So I go ahead and work. I jump in for a little more money. Them times, you know, money was money. Dollar was a dollar. Sure. So the Walter Deku line up was. Old Man Dutre on clarinet. Old Man Joe Howard on cornet. Walter Deku on piano and myself on drums. And Big Eye Louie on clarinet. Old Man Dutre is a double. Big Eye Louie couldn't double. Well, that went on…

items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: He started arranging for Papa Celestate. That's why he had put so much stuff on Ricard on the shoppers.

ctx.x: Did you ever play with Fess at all? That's right. Have you played with Fess?

I played with Fess. My first lesson I took when I was learning how to read, I went to Fess and lived on Ellick Street in Algeria. He told me to get a little Tesson's Catechism. I said, boy you done improved mighty quick on that horn. Woo woo. I said, well begin from that catechism you start from. That's all. Like the people talk about Eddie Pearson. Steve Lewis was learning how to play trombone. And Steve Lewis didn't make you, bought a brand new horn. And Eddie Pearson come to my heart and say, that was, that…
Yeah, there's so many people you know.
